facts.text: The package registers the environment as TradingEnv with entry point gym_trading_env.environments:TradingEnv
The package also registers MultiDatasetTradingEnv, a TradingEnv that switches dataset on reset
The constructor's default positions list is [0, 1]
The action space is spaces.Discrete(len(positions)): the integer action indexes the positions list
The observation space is a Box from -np.inf to +np.inf with one element per static feature plus one dynamic feature per function
A column of the DataFrame is a static feature when its name contains 'feature'
Two dynamic features are added by default: the last position taken and the real position of the portfolio
The default reward is the logarithm of the portfolio valuation at a step divided by the valuation at the previous step
Step first trades to positions[position_index] when an action is given, then advances the row index
The portfolio starts at portfolio_initial_value, 1000 by default
The episode is done when the portfolio valuation is 0 or below
The episode is truncated when the row index reaches the last row of the DataFrame
A reset sets step 0 and row index 0, and draws the position uniformly from positions when initial_position is 'random'
When windows is an integer W, the observation is a stack of the last W rows

determinism.notes: reset(seed) reseeds the environment's random generator; the market series and the trade arithmetic are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions.  The package's fake draws the initial position with Python's random.Random and upstream with numpy's generator, so a seed can pick a different position on the two

gaps: event-driven market model: one step advances one row of the supplied dataset and the interval between rows is not declared by the environment, so timestep_ms is 0
the market data, the features, the fees, the borrow interest and the reward are those of the supplied DataFrame and the user's functions: no order book, slippage, latency or market impact is modelled

the fake backend replays a fixed synthetic price series in pure Python and was not compared with the upstream environment (pandas, numpy and gymnasium are not needed by the gate): its observations and trajectories differ from a real run
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against a market
snapshot and restore are not offered: TradingEnv exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
